script: Why does Cristiano Ronaldo want some fans to get BANNED from attending matches? Back in July last year, Diogo Jota died in a car crash alongside his brother André, and he was only twenty-eight years old. One of his closest friends in the world was a player called Rúben Neves, who carried Jota's coffin at the funeral. He was so close to him that he even switched to wearing the number twenty-one for Portugal just to honor him. But last Saturday, a stadium full of strangers found a way to turn that friendship into a weapon against him. Neves was playing a Saudi Pro League match for Al-Hilal against a team called Al-Taawoun, and during the game a section of the home crowd started chanting one word at him over and over. Jota. They were shouting his dead best friend's name to try and get in his head. Neves heard it and turned toward them, clapping back sarcastically before he pointed to his own eye and then up to the sky. After the game he walked past reporters and said, I hope they don't go to pray afterwards. But the person who reacted the loudest wasn't even standing on that field. Cristiano Ronaldo, who played with both Jota and Neves for Portugal, saw the video online and he was furious. He posted that the league had to punish this, saying, 'this is no longer football, and there have to be limits.' And that's exactly why Ronaldo wants them gone for good. He thinks mocking a grieving man over his dead friend crosses a line that should cost you your seat in a stadium forever.
